name: A frontend made of cells
line: Every panel is a UI cell with its own backend, contract, node and version, discovered at run time and swapped, refused or revoked while the rest keeps running.

name: A store made of cells
line: An online store in which the catalog, cart, inventory, order saga, test payments, gateway and page are each a cell with a typed contract. Stop the leaders mid-checkout: nothing is oversold, and no order is lost or made twice.

name: References: anything to anything
line: One kind of name reaches a file on a laptop, a blob, a repo file at a commit, a node, a person, a cell op, a capability and an enterprise system. It follows moves and refuses changed bytes.

name: Render across devices
line: One image, rendered by several machines at once. The result is pixel-identical to a single-machine render.

name: Kill a node, keep the data
line: Kill the server holding the data, live. Every saved write survives, and the page proves it with a hash chain.

name: An engineering result you can re-check
line: A physics result that comes with a certificate. Re-check it in your own browser: same code, same inputs, same answer.

name: One prompt, many devices
line: Ask a question and see which device answers. When one device drops out, the answer keeps streaming from another.

name: Follow-me cell
line: A service that moves to whichever machine is closest to you, and keeps answering by the same name while it moves.

name: Playground: deploy a cell in your browser
line: Write a cell in your browser, deploy it to a real network, and call it from three languages, all within a minute.

name: A stranger gets exactly one action
line: We give you a key that does exactly one thing. Try to make it do more. Every attempt is refused, and the page shows you the rule that refused it.

name: Same data, browser and terminal, live
line: Change a value in your browser and see it change in a terminal and on a 3D factory map at the same moment. One schema, no server code.

name: Search everything you are allowed to see
line: One search box across many machines. You only get back what your key allows, and the rest never leaves the machine it lives on.

name: Any program becomes a mesh service in one command
line: Turn any open-source program into a network service with one command. Then use it from your browser: same output, byte for byte.

name: Print only through the guard
line: Send a print job straight to the printer and it is refused. Send it through the guard, which checks bounds, temperatures, material and time: the 300 C job is rejected, the safe one prints, and a replay is refused.

name: Every call leaves a receipt
line: Run 200 calls across four cells, download the receipts, and check them on any machine with no network. Edit one and the verifier names it; drop one and the chain shows the gap.

name: Shared with my devices, nobody else's
line: Enroll your laptop, phone and desktop with a pairing code; each gets a key bound to that device. A copied key file is refused, and a lost phone is revoked from the laptop while the other two keep working.

name: Sharded search: one leader per shard, rebalanced live
line: 4.6 million Wikipedia abstracts in 32 shards with 3 replicas each, one leader per shard. Kill a machine under a query loop that never stops: new leaders within one lease, replicas back to three, recall unchanged.

name: A factory line you can audit
line: A three-station line runs as a twin and drill becomes the bottleneck. Download the signed event log: your browser checks every signature and recomputes the numbers. Edit one timestamp and it names the event that broke.

name: A cell that takes its data with it
line: A notes cell moves from process A to process B while a client writes to it 20 times a second. B takes over under a higher epoch, A answers stale writes with 'moved, epoch 2', and writes sent, acknowledged and present all match.

name: Read it before you can act
line: An approve key that only works after your device signs a read receipt for the exact notice. Approve first and it is refused with the clause that refused it; open the notice and the same call goes through.

name: Edit offline, merge on reconnect
line: A laptop and a phone share a parts list. Pull the cable, edit both sides, plug it back in: both show the same list within a second, the page shows how each conflict was resolved, and both state hashes match.

name: A key with a spending limit
line: Give an agent a key worth 100 units and three cells that cost different amounts. A live meter drops with each call; at 3 left a 5-unit call is refused by a cell that has never seen the key, and splitting the key into two keys worth 100 each is refused.

name: Work that pays only when it checks out
line: A requester posts 50 jobs and two workers take them; one is rigged to answer wrong one time in ten. A cheap verifier checks every result, only a pass gets a signed single-use reward token, and the rigged worker's acceptance rate drops live.

name: Revoke once, refused everywhere
line: Six cells accept one delegated key. Press revoke and each cell turns red as it refuses, with the milliseconds since the revoke. A cut-off cell keeps serving until its 30 s freshness bound runs out, then refuses everything.

name: One struct, three nodes
line: One Rust struct becomes a typed Rust client and a generated TypeScript client. Kill one of three nodes mid-run: no write is lost, offline edits merge, two viewers see different rows, and a renamed field fails to compile in both languages.

name: Fundamentals, live
line: Ten fundamental cells on a four-node mesh: typed contracts, by_name, ce-gate, cap v3 with Via, state.store, failover, search, orch, pinned builds and wrap. Every call is a signed record.

name: Find a cell, call it
line: Ask in plain words, “turn this STL into a print-ready gcode”: search ranks the cells with their typed contracts, a language model picks one and cites its fields, the build already holds that contract as Rust, orch starts the cell where it fits and a count-1 grant allows exactly one call. Or the job goes to a board and a worker returns a signed result.
